title: The Soul's Defense against the Sword of the Devil
english: This is not the body which the Savior, having entered into the womb from the Virgin, says, 'You have brought me into the dust of death' (Ps 22:14). Perhaps he also descended into mortality and the Hades, which for us is the dust of death; for it happened in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights. Ps 22:17c–19: 'They pierced my hands and my feet' signifies the death of those coming to this, having their hands and feet dug out through the piercing of the nails. 'All my bones were counted.' All the bones of the body can be counted, if they are stripped of the joined flesh; and regarding the body of Christ, the apostles declare the bones, but his flesh is spoken of by those believing more superficially and more bodily. For the body is not the same thing: the bones hold the flesh together, and the flesh happens to be around the bones, covering them. If some fear should disturb those fleeing, the superficial believers, only the hard and zealous ones are left, as if they were counted [as remaining] having been stripped after the fleeing of the crowd. 'They understood and looked upon me; even though they did not cause my [death] to happen (for I took these things willingly), they divided my garments among themselves and cast lots upon my clothing' (Ps 22:18).

Regarding the history, the words of the Scriptures are more allegorical concerning the garments and the clothing of Jesus; for the God-Word, subsisting according to spiritual meanings, both wears and is surrounded by these. The heterodox, the executioners and the spirits of the slayer, divide the garments of the Savior. For each of them receives the words of the Scriptures, and [receives] those not [of the Scriptures], even though the seamless tunic of Jesus is seamless because it is woven; for it does not consist of joined parts but has a unified nature. And it is also from above because it is divinely inspired, woven through the Spirit; for the Scripture is from above by all power. But the Church does not divide the garments nor casts lots upon them; for she has and puts on, standing at the right hands of Jesus, a Queen clothed in golden attire, variegated. Having ascended above these garments, she will clothe herself with Jesus himself, becoming wise and powerful, possessing the wisdom and power of the Father. Ps 22:20: And doing these things...

Regarding his words: 'Do not withdraw your help from me; for if you do not help and attend to my understanding, I shall rise a third time from the dead to show the vainness of the plot against me' (Ps 21:21a).

Since the surrounding enemies, seeking to kill, possess a sword capable of wounding not the body but the soul, he asks to be saved from these blades, kept unharmed from disturbance and cowardice (Ps 21:21a). For even if our soul has been sufficiently prepared, seeing the devil with the whole phalanx of demons and the swarm of opposing and evil human energies acting through them, it becomes disturbed (for its nature is changeable) and calls upon the One capable of saving from the enemy's sword.
Perhaps even the devil himself is allegorically called a sword, since he dares to wound every soul by pre-meditation; thus, he asks to be saved from this sword.

He does not previously call the dogs surrounding him in the plural, but now calls them in the singular because of their kind (Ps 21:21b). And his soul is called 'only-begotten' because it is isolated and separated from all other souls; for all those there have known sin, but this one has not. And while God the Word visits those others at intervals, this one remains unseparated and indivisible without distinction until the end. Because of these exceptional qualities, he is called his only-begotten.

Perhaps also the glorious church standing before him, having no flaw or wrinkle and being filled by the blameless and perfect, is his only-begotten, though progressing into many ranks divided by the difference in progress: sixty indeed of queens, and eighty of companions and maidens whose number is countless; one of them is a perfect dove above all, an only-begotten one to her mother, the upper Jerusalem.

He asks to be saved now from the devil, previously spoken of as a lion, but also through his own humiliation, by which he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross (Ps 21:22). And he wishes to be saved also from the horns of the unicorns, which are an opposing power promising a kingdom; for the horn is a symbol of a kingdom. And those who consider the...

title: The Two Kinds of Wealth and Prayer
english: To signify a cross from the preceding word, having the shape of a horn (Ps 21:23).

The Epistle to the Hebrews says that this word is spoken from the person of Christ, as he says to the Father: 'O Father, your own name, that is, your own property and peculiarity, I will declare, making it manifest to my brothers who were born of me, to whom you sent my spirit; to whom it will be said, What you are, God sent the spirit of his Son into your hearts. For they are not those who have received the spirit of adoption from God, so as to be sons of God and brothers of the only-begotten. And having indeed risen from the dead, having appeared to the women, he says, "I have gone to my brothers." And in the midst of this gathering assembly, he will sing praise to the Father, sending up theological thoughts and songs.'

In many ways he is called Jacob (for the typology signifies this: when he is the divine man, the son of Isaac, the father of the twelve patriarchs; when he is the twelve-tribed people proceeding from him; when he is the ten tribes alone having split from David and having followed Jeroboam; when he is the savior himself, 'Jacob my servant, I will take hold of him'; 'Israel my chosen one, my soul has received him'; for Matthew wrote this prophecy concerning the Savior), it should be sought why it is said, 'O all the seed of Jacob, glorify him' (Ps 21:24). And one might say: the twelve-tribed seed of the patriarch Jacob, having been immersed in the reading of the law and the prophets, wishes to glorify God also through thoughts and words and good works. But perhaps, since this is a falsehood, many of those descended from Jacob being unfaithful and traitors to Jesus, someone will say: what [is said of] the seed of Jacob the 'plucked-up' and 'beaten-down' by death and the opposing power (and Jesus is that [seed]), his seed who came from teaching, will be able to glorify God. And since Israel is also the one whom the soul of God has received, the chosen seed of his, Israel will fear God. And each of those imitating...

If Jesus has a struggle against the principalities, powers, and rulers of this darkness, Jacob is one who beats back the opponents; but if he has a pure heart and a clear mind, he will see God, Israel being such a person. No seed of such a person will fail to fear God.

Since he did not reject the prayer of me the poor man nor crush it (Ps 21:25), for this reason, becoming thankful that the prayer for us was heard by the Lord, you praised, glorified, and feared him. For even though I prayed to him as a poor man, but you ought to know what I am: a rich man, a treasure of the fullness of goods; through you I became poor so that through my poverty I might make you rich; for those who are surrounded by the flesh did not receive my wealth, knowing and prophesying only a part of it. Having become poor for you, I cried out to the Lord on your behalf, and he heard me, giving you those things by which you were found rich. For in my interceding for you, he did not turn his face away from me, but rather he shone it upon me; therefore he also applied his attention to my cry.

Men indeed praise based on visible works and conveniences, but God, seeing the hidden, praises based on perfect virtue and surpassing knowledge (Ps 21:26a). It is not for anyone to say with boldness: 'O God, my praise is from you, not based on chance things, but on a great assembly'; for a great assembly is the one gathered from the great according to their kind, just as a great assembly is the one gathered from many (Ps 21:26b).

A prayer is a confession made in thanksgiving, if one should obtain these things from God (Ps 21:27). Concerning the two kinds of wealth, as the Scriptures say, to be the one rich in good works and in every word and in all knowledge, and the other to be rich from false-glorious dogmas and unpleasant deeds, being a poverty contrary to each kind of wealth. And he who possesses the divine wealth, being deprived of the worthless, possesses the contrary poverty, yet as a rich man and a poor man, I praise him as being such; just as he who possesses the laborious wealth possesses also the false poverty opposed to the wealth that...

title: The Spiritual Worship of the Poor
english: Concerning those who labor not in a praiseworthy way, the saying 'The poor shall eat and be filled' is spoken. But you say 'the poor' according to the saying, meaning those from the nations who previously had no hope and were atheists in the world, who are coming to faith and shall eat and be filled (Ps 22:28). Remembering God at the ends of the earth and turning from the nations, those who have passed from the earth shall have their citizenship in heaven. And all the families of the nations shall worship before Him.

The Jews also seemed to worship before God coming to Jerusalem and the temple which Solomon built. This typical worship in a place, however, is not what the nations dwelling even unto the ends of the earth are to perform; rather, they were taught to worship in spirit and truth, remaining where they are, performing worship before God, as God wills them to live as citizens. With this, the prophecy also agrees, saying: 'And all the islands of the nations shall worship before Him, every place from its own place,' as Zephaniah says (Zeph 3:9).

Those nourished in the earth can be 'poor of the earth' (Ps 22:27), those who, having been called to repentance in spirit, are killing the deeds of the body so as to no longer think of earthly things, having eaten the spiritual food offered by Jesus, worshipped God in spirit and truth. And it is possible to call 'poor of the earth' those on earth who are departing from worldly wisdom, those becoming rich and ruling sensually; for these, having eaten the food from Jesus, being not a remedy for those foreseeing evils, shall worship God, finding Him above all wisdom, wealth, and rule.

But descending into the earth, if anyone is like those angels descending from heaven to earth and worshipping the Lord and Savior, according to 'Let all the angels of God worship Him' (Ps 97:7); but He stood ready if those receiving common death can descend into the earth, some of whom shall worship the Lord on behalf of them, having become in the lower parts of the earth (Ps 22:30c, 31a). But he said well that his own soul lives for him, and not that it serves him; but that the seed shall serve him. For the nature that was taken was united to the divinity that took hold of it, and partook of the same glory and honor.

Ps 21:31b-32: 'A generation goes and a generation comes' (Eccl 1:4)—some take it of the two peoples: they have called those of the circumcision the departing generation, because they have turned away from the Lord, having become 'a crooked and perverse generation' (Deut 32:5).
And the coming generation is the calling from the nations, hastening to the very Savior who calls.

This one, then, will be announced to the Lord by the ambassadors on her behalf, saying: 'To you nations shall come from the end of the earth' (Jer 16:19), and 'All the nations, as many as you have made, shall come and worship before you' (Ps 85:9).
For the Savior who says, 'The one coming to me I will not cast out' (John 6:37), does not cast out this coming generation.
And it is well said 'the one coming' and not 'the one who has come'; for he does not cast out the one who is always effecting his coming to him by practicing the things of virtue.
And the generation of which the discourse speaks has not come but is coming to him, cherishing the things of faith.

And these same ones who announce to the Lord the coming generation also announce God's righteousness through faith in Jesus, effected in all who believe, to the people to be born, a divine offspring, whom the Lord made, having acquired it through his own blood, calling the not-people his people (Hos 2:25; Rom 9:25).

Ps 22:1b-3a: The one who, through attaining the meek and well-ordered, has been named a sheep of Christ will say concerning the good shepherd: 'The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing' (Ps 22:1).
For he leads me to the saving pasture, where there are divine grasses, concerning which the shepherd himself says of his own sheep: 'He shall go in and go out and find pasture' (John 10:9).
And the place of green grass can be the divine instruction, where spiritual grass is found, being ethical teaching.
In this place, then, 'he made me dwell'—not 'he settled me'; for he wants me, as far as I progress, to use such pasture perfectly.
For having become from a sheep a man, I shall be tried no longer by a shepherd but by a trainer and teacher.
'He nourished me by water of rest' (Ps 22:2). For the ethical lesson is not only a cure for thirst, but also provides release from sins.
'He converted my soul' (Ps 22:3); for even if, being a sheep, I have strayed outside [...].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
